info.title: Node.js canonical path symlink resolution setup

diffs.patch:
Index: bin/resolve-real-path.js
===================================================================
--- bin/resolve-real-path.js	
+++ bin/resolve-real-path.js	
@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env node
+'use strict'
+
+const resolveRealPath = require('../index.js')
+
+const target = process.argv[2]
+
+if (!target) {
+  console.error('Usage: resolve-real-path <path>')
+  process.exit(1)
+}
+
+try {
+  process.stdout.write(resolveRealPath(target) + '\n')
+} catch (err) {
+  console.error('resolve-real-path: ' + err.message)
+  process.exit(1)
+}

Index: index.js
===================================================================
--- index.js	
+++ index.js	
@@ -0,0 +1,13 @@
+'use strict'
+
+const fs = require('fs')
+
+function resolveRealPath(inputPath) {
+  if (typeof fs.realpathSync.native === 'function') {
+    return fs.realpathSync.native(inputPath)
+  }
+  return fs.realpathSync(inputPath)
+}
+
+module.exports = resolveRealPath
+module.exports.resolveRealPath = resolveRealPath

Index: package.json
===================================================================
--- package.json	
+++ package.json	
@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+{
+  "name": "resolve-real-path",
+  "version": "1.0.0",
+  "description": "Resolve symlinks in a path to its canonical filesystem path, consistently across Node.js versions.",
+  "main": "index.js",
+  "bin": {
+    "resolve-real-path": "bin/resolve-real-path.js"
+  },
+  "files": [
+    "index.js",
+    "bin/"
+  ],
+  "scripts": {
+    "test": "node test/index.test.js"
+  },
+  "engines": {
+    "node": ">=8"
+  },
+  "license": "MIT"
+}

Index: test/index.test.js
===================================================================
--- test/index.test.js	
+++ test/index.test.js	
@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
+'use strict'
+
+const assert = require('assert')
+const fs = require('fs')
+const os = require('os')
+const path = require('path')
+const resolveRealPath = require('../index.js')
+
+function canonical(p) {
+  return typeof fs.realpathSync.native === 'function'
+    ? fs.realpathSync.native(p)
+    : fs.realpathSync(p)
+}
+
+function removeDir(dir) {
+  if (typeof fs.rmSync === 'function') {
+    fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })
+  } else {
+    fs.rmdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })
+  }
+}
+
+const tmp = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'resolve-real-path-'))
+
+try {
+  const realDir = path.join(tmp, 'real')
+  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(realDir, 'nested'), { recursive: true })
+  const link = path.join(tmp, 'link')
+  fs.symlinkSync(realDir, link, 'dir')
+
+  assert.strictEqual(resolveRealPath(link), canonical(realDir))
+  assert.strictEqual(
+    resolveRealPath(path.join(link, 'nested')),
+    canonical(path.join(realDir, 'nested'))
+  )
+
+  const dirA = path.join(tmp, 'a')
+  const dirB = path.join(tmp, 'b')
+  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(dirA, 'real'), { recursive: true })
+  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(dirA, 'sibling'), { recursive: true })
+  fs.mkdirSync(dirB)
+  const linkB = path.join(dirB, 'link')
+  fs.symlinkSync(path.join(dirA, 'real'), linkB, 'dir')
+
+  assert.strictEqual(
+    resolveRealPath(linkB + path.sep + '..' + path.sep + 'sibling'),
+    canonical(path.join(dirA, 'sibling'))
+  )
+
+  const relative = path.relative(process.cwd(), link)
+  assert.strictEqual(resolveRealPath(relative), canonical(realDir))
+
+  console.log('ok')
+} finally {
+  removeDir(tmp)
+}

Interesting! `fs.realpathSync.native` resolved `/b/link/../sibling` to `/b/sibling` (lexically) rather than physically following the symlink. Wait the error shows path `/tmp/.../b/sibling` - so native resolved `link/..` lexically to `b`, then sibling doesn't exist. Hmm, that's the native behavior on Linux? Actually POSIX realpath does resolve `..` after symlinks. Let me think.

Wait, actually the issue: On Linux, `realpath(3)` should resolve `/b/link/../sibling`: link -> /a/real, so /b/link/.. = /a, then /a/sibling exists. But Node's native returned /b/sibling. That suggests Node's `.native` uses `uv_fs_realpath` which... hmm. Or maybe glibc's realpath in older versions resolved `..` lexically! Yes! This is a known thing: glibc's `realpath` implementation historically resolved `..` lexically rather than physically in some cases? Actually no.

Hmm, wait. Let me reconsider. Actually there IS a well-known discrepancy: Node's JS `fs.realpath` implementation resolves symlinks correctly for `..`, while the native `realpath(3)` on some platforms/glibc versions resolves `..` lexically. Actually I recall the opposite.

Let me actually test with the JS implementation to compare. The test shows native gives /b/sibling. Let me test fs.realpathSync (JS) on the same path.

This is actually the crux of "works consistently across Node versions" — the native vs JS implementations differ! Ugh. So preferring native isn't necessarily more correct.

Hmm, but for a "real, canonical filesystem path", the physical resolution (`/a/sibling`) is arguably correct. But what does the OS/realpath define? POSIX realpath: "the pathname shall be resolved ... All components of the pathname shall be examined ... symbolic links shall be resolved." The handling of `..` after a symlink: POSIX says realpath resolves symlinks then processes `..`? Actually POSIX says the `..` is resolved based on the symlink target (physical). glibc realpath does physical. So why did native give /b/sibling?

Wait, maybe I mis-set up. `fs.symlinkSync(path.join(dirA, 'real'), linkB, 'dir')` — linkB = tmp/b/link -> tmp/a/real. Then `path.join(linkB, '..', 'sibling')` = tmp/b/link/../sibling. Node's native realpath... Let me actually check what happens. Maybe Node normalizes the path string before calling native? Node does `path.resolve`? No.

Actually! I bet `path.join` normalized `link/../sibling` to `tmp/b/sibling` lexically before it even got passed! Yes! `path.join` collapses `..` segments lexically. `path.join('/b/link', '..', 'sibling')` = `/b/sibling`. So the test itself is flawed, not the implementation. I should construct the path with string concatenation to preserve `..`.

So the implementation is likely fine. Let me fix the test to build the path without `path.join` normalization: `linkB + path.sep + '..' + path.sep + 'sibling'`.

Good catch. Let me fix.
The failure is in my test, not the implementation: `path.join` collapses `..` lexically before the path is passed. Building the string manually preserves the physical symlink traversal.
